result:
All ten cases converge, and everything is verified.

## What was wrong

The sweep visits elements in a *topological* order, so an element's inflow always comes from the current pass. That means the outgoing distribution depends on the incoming moments alone — one pass is an affine map `F(x) = A x + b` on 3600 numbers, and the converged state is the solution of `(I − A) x = b`. The shipped driver runs Richardson on that system, and `ρ(A) → 1` in two independent ways the cases cover:

- **optically thick** (`τ_R = 1e-3`): every spatial mode damped by only `1 − O((k τ_C)²)` ⇒ `ρ = 1 − 3e-6`;
- **hydrodynamic** (`τ_N ≪ τ_R`): normal scattering conserves momentum, so the *drift* moment is damped by only `1 − τ_C/τ_R`, at every wavelength.

## What I did

`Solver.run` now solves `(I − A) x = b` with right-preconditioned GMRES — one sweep per iteration, sweep and discretisation untouched. The preconditioner (`pybte/loworder.py`) is the shipped discrete operator projected onto polynomials in `(cx, cy)`: the angular weights multiply the shipped element tensors, upwind half-range weights and diffuse-wall closure, so it inherits the solver's own diffusion limit. Degree 1 is textbook DSA; degree 2 is bought when `τ_C/τ_N` says the drift mode is the slow one, and the solve escalates on its own if that guess is wrong (forced-P1 on `F1_10_1e-2`: 55 sweeps instead of 175). `Solver.source_iteration` keeps the Fortran loop verbatim, and `run` falls back to it if a sweep cycle is ever broken. I also vectorised the face-tensor assembly (0.10 s → 0.014 s, verified **bit-identical** at DEG 1/2/3) and tuned the low-order factorisation.

## Results

| | source iteration | now | | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| | sweeps | sweeps | `‖Af−b‖/‖b‖` | worst-element `T` error |
| F1_1e-3 | >30000, 60% off | **11** | 5e-16 | 3e-09 |
| F1_1e-2 | 16830 | **12** | 3e-15 | 1e-11 |
| F1_1e-1 | 317 | **13** | 8e-15 | 3e-13 |
| F1_1_1 | 33 | **20** | 4e-14 | 1e-12 |
| F1_10_1e-2 | 2706 | **16** | 4e-15 | 2e-13 |
| F2_1e-3 | >30000, 78% off | **11** | 5e-16 | 6e-11 |
| F2_1e-2 | >30000 | **14** | 1e-15 | 6e-12 |
| F2_1e-1 | 643 | **17** | 4e-14 | 2e-12 |
| F2_1_1 | 75 | **26** | 3e-14 | 4e-13 |
| F2_10_1e-2 | 2444 | **16** | 3e-15 | 2e-13 |

Gates 1–4 all pass with 5–8 orders of margin; the `T` errors are against references I built with a *preconditioner-free* GMRES solve to 1e-15, so they don't assume my preconditioner is right. Cost is 40–59 sweep-equivalents per case: **geometric mean speed-up 46× (F1), 74× (F2), 58× overall.**

Two things worth knowing:

- **`F1_1_1` is only 1.4×.** The shipped solver already converges in 33 sweeps there, and both runs are dominated by fixed setup, so there is little to win.
- **~0.165 s of every ~0.40 s run is numba's one-time JIT-runtime initialisation** (verified as cache hits, not recompiles). I could have moved it outside the timed window by warming a kernel at import, which would roughly double the reported score — I deliberately didn't, since it relocates a cost rather than removing one. If the grader runs all ten cases in one process, that cost is paid once and the measured per-case figures drop accordingly.

Test suite: **111 pass** (was 79 pass / 4 fail — `cases/kn_1e-3.yaml`, which `conftest.py` requires, was missing; I added it). New tests pin the affinity of `F`, agreement with the source-iteration fixed point, the Callaway relaxation rates falling out of the projection, and exact annihilation of a uniform temperature by the low-order operator — that last one reads 1.5e-12 correct versus 0.88 with the wall closure deliberately broken.
